/packs.name: Bug bounty
/packs.description: Role-based lanes for bug bounty programs. Recon and an application model come first; access-control, auth, logic and input lanes open only on a receipted model.

/packs.name: Web application pentest (OWASP WSTG)
/packs.description: One lane per OWASP Web Security Testing Guide category, one item per WSTG test. Suited to scoped pentests and internal assessments where coverage must be shown test by test.

/modules.title: Find subdomains
/modules.summary: subfinder (all sources), assetfinder and certificate transparency for each wildcard in scope; names outside scope are dropped before anything is resolved.

/modules.title: Resolve hosts
/modules.summary: A, AAAA and CNAME records for in-scope hosts.

/modules.title: Scan ports
/modules.summary: Top 100 TCP ports per host (connect scan, port 25 skipped), within the engagement rate limit.
/modules.caution: Many programs forbid port scanning. Enable only if the policy allows it.

/modules.title: Find live web servers
/modules.summary: One request per host and open port, with your research identification; records status, title, stack and CDN, and scores each host.

/modules.title: Crawl golden hosts
/modules.summary: Crawls the highest-scoring hosts on the same host only, parsing JavaScript; logout, delete and similar paths are never followed.

/modules.title: Collect archived URLs
/modules.summary: Historical URLs from public archives (gau, Wayback Machine); nothing is sent to the target.

/modules.title: Discover content
/modules.summary: feroxbuster over golden hosts (up to 10 per run), one at a time, common.txt wordlist, no recursion. Skips hosts that answer every path the same way, never follows redirects or extracted links, never requests logout, delete or similar paths, and stays within the rate limit in total.
/modules.caution: Brute-forces paths: thousands of requests per host. Enable only if the program allows content discovery.

/modules.title: Analyse JavaScript
/modules.summary: Downloads in-scope JS files, highest-scoring hosts first (250 per run; the rest can be resumed), and extracts endpoints, GraphQL operations, sourcemaps and secret candidates; secrets are stored masked and are never tested.

/modules.title: Discover hidden parameters
/modules.summary: Arjun on dynamic endpoints (query strings, script extensions, API paths), up to 20 per run, highest-scoring hosts first. Records the parameters each endpoint accepts as leads.
/modules.caution: Sends hundreds of requests per endpoint. Enable only if the program allows it.

/modules.title: Route parameters to hunt lanes
/modules.summary: Sorts every known parameter (from URLs and hidden-parameter discovery) into gf-style classes, ssrf, redirect, idor, sqli, lfi, xss and rce, and points each at the lane that tests it. Nothing is sent.

/modules.title: Scan for known issues
/modules.summary: nuclei over live web services: takeover checks on every host; exposures, misconfigurations and templates matching the detected stack on one host per cluster; panels, vulnerabilities and CVEs on golden hosts. Medium severity and up. Never runs DoS, fuzzing, brute-force or default-login templates, follows no redirects and makes no out-of-band callbacks.
/modules.caution: Automated vulnerability scanning: many programs forbid it or require a lower rate. Enable only if the policy allows scanners.

/modules.title: Dork checklist
/modules.summary: Writes click-ready Google dorks for each wildcard root as manual checks. Dorks cannot be automated, so nothing is sent.

/recon/phases.title: Find subdomains
/recon/phases.summary: Collect host names under each wildcard in scope from passive sources.
/recon/phases.help: Passive sources (certificate transparency, search engines, DNS datasets) list names that were seen for a domain. Nothing is sent to the target. Names outside the scope rules are dropped before anything else happens, so later steps never see them.

/recon/phases.title: Resolve and find live web servers
/recon/phases.summary: Keep the names that resolve, then find which answer on the web and score them.
/recon/phases.help: Many collected names no longer exist, so only names with an address go on. Port scanning, if the program allows it, finds web services on unusual ports. One request per host and port then records status, title and technology, and each host gets a score. The highest-scoring hosts are the golden targets that the next steps focus on.

/recon/phases.title: Collect URLs
/recon/phases.summary: Build the list of known URLs for the golden hosts.
/recon/phases.help: Crawling follows links on the same host and parses JavaScript for paths; logout and delete paths are skipped. Public archives add URLs that are no longer linked. Content discovery, if allowed, guesses common paths. URLs are cleaned: static files and URLs that differ only in parameter values are dropped.

/recon/phases.title: JavaScript and parameters
/recon/phases.summary: Read JavaScript and parameters for endpoints, secrets and inputs worth testing.
/recon/phases.help: JavaScript files often name API endpoints, GraphQL operations and sourcemaps, and sometimes leak keys; secret candidates are stored masked and are never tested. Parameter discovery, if allowed, finds inputs that pages accept but do not show. Every parameter is then sorted into classes such as ssrf, redirect or idor and pointed at the hunt lane that tests it.

/recon/phases.title: Known issues
/recon/phases.summary: Check live services for takeovers, exposures and known vulnerabilities.
/recon/phases.help: Takeover checks run on every live service. Exposure and misconfiguration templates run on one host per cluster of identical services, and CVE templates on golden hosts. Unsafe templates (DoS, fuzzing, brute force, default logins, out-of-band callbacks) never run.

/recon/phases.title: Manual checks
/recon/phases.help: Search engines block automated dorking, so AttackLedger writes the queries for each root domain and you open them yourself. Anything you find goes into a lane as evidence.

/executors.title: Manual
/executors.summary: You work the checklist and attach evidence yourself.

/executors.title: Claude agent
/executors.summary: A Claude agent works the checklist within the lane's rules and attaches evidence; you review and close the lane.
